HAP1 CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screen: count table

Source: R/hap1_data.R
hap1_count_table.Rd

sgRNA read counts of a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 knockout screen in HAP1 cells with the TKOv3 library (Hart et al. 2017): the T0 sample and three replicates after 3 and 18 days of growth. The sgRNAs of the genes needed for growth (essential genes) are depleted over time. It is the example dataset of the CRISPR tutorial.

Usage

data(hap1_count_table)

Format

A data frame with 13600 rows (sgRNAs) and 8 columns:

Barcode

The sgRNA identifier (gene and guide sequence).

T0

The counts at the start of the screen.

T3_A, T3_B, T3_C

The counts of the three replicates after 3 days.

T18_A, T18_B, T18_C

The counts after 18 days.

Source

Hart T, Tong AHY, Chan K, et al. (2017). Evaluation and design of genome-wide CRISPR/SpCas9 knockout screens. G3 7:2719-2727. doi:10.1534/g3.117.041277

Details

To keep the package small, the dataset is a subset of the library (70,877 sgRNAs, 4 for each of about 18,000 genes): all the sgRNAs of the core essential and non-essential reference genes (hart_reference_genes), all the sgRNAs on chromosome 15, the sgRNAs of 1500 other randomly chosen genes and the control sgRNAs (EGFP, LacZ, luciferase). Because it is a subset, it must not be used with correct_crispr_bias, which needs the complete library. The script that builds it is in the scripts folder of the installed package (system.file("scripts", package = "ScreenR")).

The data come from the example data of BAGEL2 (https://github.com/hart-lab/bagel), distributed under the MIT license, Copyright (c) 2020 Hart Lab (see system.file("LICENSES_data.txt", package = "ScreenR")).

See also

hap1_annotation_table, hart_reference_genes

Examples

data(hap1_count_table)
head(hap1_count_table)
